## read all data

```{r all data}
# read & stack
N2OIEF <- list.files("Output", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE) %>% 
  # iterate over each file and bind rows as we go
  map_dfr(~ {
    file    <- .x
    raw_tbl <- read_csv(file, show_col_types = FALSE)

    # 1. harmonise key columns --------------------------------------------------
   clean_tbl <- raw_tbl %>%
   rename_with(~ "Region", any_of(c("Province", "ProvinceID", "Region"))) %>% 
   rename_with(~ "Crop",   any_of(c("Crop", "CropID")))

    # 2. add metadata -----------------------------------------------------------
    clean_tbl %>% 
      mutate(
        File      = basename(file),
        Country   = str_detect(File, "_Canada")   %>% if_else("Canada", "USA"),
        Pathway   = case_when(
          str_detect(File, "FSN")            ~ "Direct – FSN",
          str_detect(File, "Irrigation")     ~ "Direct – Irrigation",
          str_detect(File, "Volatilization") ~ "Indirect – Volatilisation",
          str_detect(File, "Leaching")       ~ "Indirect – Leaching",
          TRUE                               ~ "Unknown"
        )
      ) %>% 
      # 3. keep only what we need (Region, Crop, N2O.IEF + metadata)
      select(Region, Crop, N2O.IEF, Country, Pathway, File)
  }) %>%
  mutate(N2O.IEF = na_if(N2O.IEF,0)) %>%
  mutate(IsDirect = str_starts(Pathway, "Direct"))

# Replace Canada's region name
N2OIEF <- N2OIEF %>%
   mutate(
    Region = case_when(
      Country == "Canada" & Region == "QC" ~ "QUEBEC",
      Country == "Canada" & Region == "ON" ~ "ONTARIO",
      Country == "Canada" & Region == "MB" ~ "MANITOBA",
      Country == "Canada" & Region == "SK" ~ "SASKATCHEWAN",
      Country == "Canada" & Region == "AB" ~ "ALBERTA",
      Country == "Canada" & Region == "BC" ~ "BRITISH COLUMBIA",
      Country == "Canada" & Region == "AT" ~ "ATLANTIC",         # special case
      TRUE                                   ~ Region            # keep other values
    ))

# Sum of Direct and indirect
N2OIEF <- N2OIEF %>%
  group_by(Region,Country,IsDirect)%>%
  summarise()


```


## Plot 

X xais is the State/Canad'a region and Y axis is the N2OIEF
The most left region has the lowest sum of direct IEF, and the most right one has the highest sum of direct IEF.

## Plot distribution of crop's N2OIEF

```{r distribution plot}

#  prepare data: drop missing emission-factors
df <- N2OIEF %>% 
  filter(!is.na(N2O.IEF))%>%
  mutate(LogIEF = log10(N2O.IEF)) %>%
  mutate(Crop = factor(Crop, levels = rev(sort(unique(Crop)))))

#Plot ridge plot
library(ggridges)
library(forcats)

p <- df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = LogIEF, y = Crop, fill = Pathway)) +
  geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_x_continuous("Log10 implied N2O emission factor") +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Helvetica", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.title     = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.text      = element_text(size = 6),
    strip.text     = element_text(size = 7, face = "bold"),
    legend.text    = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.title   = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.position= "bottom"
  )


# after building your ggplot object `p`:
ggsave(
  filename = "Figures/Fig1_IEF_ridgelines.pdf",
  plot     = p,
  # 2-column width = 180 mm → 180/25.4 ≈ 7.09 in
  width    = 7.09,  
  height   = 8.27,  # e.g. max 2-col height ~210 mm → 210/25.4 ≈ 8.27 in
  units    = "in",
  device   = cairo_pdf  # embeds fonts cleanly
)


```
